decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 75 basis points to a range of 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: Overall economic activity appears to have picked up after edging down in the first quarter.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledges that the economy rebounded after shrinking at the start of the year.

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate.
changes.explanation: The Fed raised rates significantly higher than the previous range and signaled that more rate hikes are coming.

changes.quote: The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
changes.explanation: A new sentence emphasizing their unwavering dedication to bringing high inflation back down to their official target.

changes.quote: In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in May.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its language to confirm it is actively shrinking its bond portfolio according to previously announced plans.

changes.quote: Voting against this action was Esther L. George, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 0.5 percentage point to 1-1/4 percent to 1-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: One official dissented, preferring a smaller rate hike of 50 basis points instead of the 75 basis point increase.

tone_quotes.quote: Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 14.56% APR, a 75 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $3.12.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.33% and moved -16 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.09% would fall by about $29.35 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $45.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 366k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 8.5% over the past year (May 2022); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 5.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -25 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.46%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.02% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that policymakers intend to keep pushing interest rates higher to tackle strong price pressures. As an educational note, the forecast model assigns a 100% probability of another rate hike at the upcoming meeting.
